summary.headline: Words review: family and their jobs, cousins and relatives, ages (bent / sabiyye / mara / 5ityaara), professions

rules.title: Cousins: one = eben 3am / bent 3am, more than one = wlaad 3am / banaat 3am
bullets: wlaad is the plural used for eben here; abnaa2 is fus7a and never used.
Mother's side the same way: eben 5aal, banaat 5aal u 5aale.
2araayeb = relatives; one relative is 2areeb, the same word as 'close'.

examples.line: kam eben 3am 3indak - how many cousins do you have
We say ولاد عم. بس when we say one we say ابن عم
5ames banaat 3am u tese3 wlaad 3am - five female cousins and nine male cousins
3indi etna3sh banaat 5aal u 5aale, u e7da3sh eben 5aal u 5aale - twelve female and eleven male cousins on my mother's side

rules.title: Ages: bent -> sabiyye -> mara -> 5ityaara (f); walad -> shab -> zalame -> 5ityaar (m)
rules.pattern: iza ... 3omorha a2al min ... betkoon ...  |  bein ... u ... bitkoon ...  |  aktar min ... bitkoon ...
bullets: Under about 14 a girl is bent; 20-30 sabiyye; 30-60 mara; over 60 5ityaara.
A boy is walad; 13-30 shab; 30-60 zalame; over 60 5ityaar.

examples.line: iza benet 3omorha a2al min arba3ta3sh, betkoon benet - if a girl is under fourteen she is a bent
u bein 3eshreen u talateen bitkoon sabiyye - between twenty and thirty she is a sabiyye
bein talateen u sitteen bitkoon mara u aktar min sitteen bitkoon 5ityaar - 30-60 a mara, over 60 a 5ityaar(a)
a2al min e7da3sh el-walad beykoon walad, bein talatta3sh u talateen beykoon shab, u bein talateen u sitteen bikoon zalame
